problem: Every merge to main launched deployment, browser readback, memory, SEO and security workflows even when the commit only changed documentation, learning, tests or agent skills.
root_cause: Several post-merge workflows used unscoped push:main triggers, and CodeQL used run_id as its push concurrency identity. This converted harmless governance/writeback merges into new production deployments and non-coalescing runner demand.
prevention: Production deploy/readback skips commits whose entire delta is docs, tests, GitHub workflow governance, agent skills or Brain learning.
Canonical shell and SEO post-merge workflows use domain path scopes.
Shared Agent Memory remains a pre-merge/change-scoped authority and does not rerun on every main push.
CodeQL main pushes are code-scoped and stale same-ref scans use cancel-in-progress with stable ref identity.
Main Write Integrity remains intentionally unscoped because every main write requires provenance observation.
Any commit containing both ignored governance files and runtime files still triggers production delivery.
